hook_text: A 5 litre pot of soup and a pile of 250 millilitre cups. How many players get soup? No long division allowed.
clip_script: Soccer tournament in Mthatha. The kitchen has a 5 litre pot of soup and cups that hold 250 millilitres. A quarter of a litre, because 1 000 divided by 4 is 250. So 4 cups fill 1 litre. 5 litres? 5 times 4: 20 cups, 20 players fed. Check: 20 times 250 is 5 000 millilitres, exactly 5 litres. Now the juice: 2 litres 500 millilitres plus 750 millilitres. Millilitres first: 2 500 plus 750 is 3 250, which is 3 litres 250 millilitres. And watch the zeros: 1 litre 50 millilitres is 1 050, not 1 500.
visual_style: Whiteboard soup pot pouring into cups in groups of four per litre; juice bottles adding in millilitres; a zero being placed carefully.
pacing: The soup puzzle, the four-cups-per-litre trick, a fast addition, then the zero trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how many cups your family's kettle can fill.
